data.content: ## Review — ENG-1099: show responsibilities on facility users list **Scope reviewed:** uncommitted working-tree changes to [src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx) and [src/types/user/user.ts](src/types/user/user.ts). The branch has no commits ahead of `develop`, so this is the whole change. --- ## Lens 1 — Intent & legibility **What it does:** `UserCard`'s footer now renders up to two role-organization ("Responsibility") badges on the left, a `+N More` control when there are more, and moves the existing actions + "See Details" button into a right-aligned group. The type change moves `role_orgs` from `UserRead` down to `UserReadMinimal`. **Why:** so staff can see a user's responsibility assignments from the users list without opening each profile. **Confidence:** high. Entry = card render; exit = badge row; no state, no new requests; empty `role_orgs` degrades cleanly (`justify-between` keeps actions right-aligned). ### ✅ The type move is correct I verified against the backend: `UserSpec` (the read/list spec, used by `FacilityUsersViewSet.pydantic_read_model`) already serializes `role_orgs` via `get_cached_role_orgs()` — it is not exclusive to `UserRetrieveSpec`. So `role_orgs` genuinely belongs on `UserReadMinimal`, and the facility users list response will contain it. No extra query, no N+1 (it's a cached column). Good. ### `Broken` — the `+N More` button's accessible name contradicts its visible label ```tsx aria-label={t("see_details")} ``` The visible text is `+2 More`; the accessible name is "See Details". That's a WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) failure — voice-control users saying "click plus two more" get nothing — and it puts **two buttons named "See Details"** in the same card for a screen-reader user, with no way to tell them apart. Per [careui.instructions.md](.github/instructions/careui.instructions.md) (ARIA + accessible names). If this stays a button, give it a name that matches what's shown. If it becomes a plain badge (see Lens 2), the problem disappears. ### Secondary — shared-component blast radius `UserCard` is consumed by three call sites, and all three now get the badges: - [FacilityOrganizationUsers.tsx](src/pages/Facility/settings/organizations/FacilityOrganizationUsers.tsx#L160) — the ticket's target - [OrganizationUsers.tsx](src/pages/Organization/OrganizationUsers.tsx#L213) — **every user listed here is already a member of the organization being viewed**, so its own name will be one of the two badges shown. That's a wasted slot on the page where it's least informative. - [UserGrid](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx#L177) (facility users card view) Was the organization-users page intended to change too? If not, gate it with a prop. If yes, consider filtering out the currently-viewed organization so the two visible slots carry new information. --- ## Lens 2 — Approach & simplicity ### The `+N More` button duplicates the button sitting right next to it Both `+N More` and `See Details` call `navigate(userDetailsPath)`. Two controls, one card, identical behaviour — that's an extra interactive element that adds no capability, and it's the direct cause of the `aria-label` collision above. There's already a precedent in this repo for exactly this pattern, and it uses a **non-interactive** overflow indicator — [ServicePointsDropDown.tsx](src/pages/Facility/queues/ServicePointsDropDown.tsx#L74-L81): ```tsx {activeServicePointCount > defaultServicePoints && ( {"+"} {t("count_more", { count: ... })} )} ``` Matching that would be strictly less code, remove the a11y issue, and fix the sizing bug in Lens 3 in one go: ```tsx {additionalResponsibilities > 0 && ( +{t("count_more", { count: additionalResponsibilities })} )} ``` If you *do* want the remaining names reachable from the list, a `Tooltip`/`Popover` listing them beats a round trip to the detail page — but a plain span is the smaller, consistent change and I'd start there. ### `Polish` - `className="w-auto"` on `Badge` is a no-op — `Badge` is `inline-flex`, which is already auto-width. - `userDetailsPath` wraps a complete ternary in a redundant template literal; `const userDetailsPath = facility ? \`/facility/${facility}/users/${user.username}\` : \`/users/${user.username}\`;` reads cleaner. (Inherited from the original inline expression, so optional.) - *Out of scope:* the inline `role_orgs` element type in [user.ts](src/types/user/user.ts#L28) duplicates `RoleOrgMembership` in [UserRoleOrganizationAccess.tsx](src/components/Users/UserRoleOrganizationAccess.tsx#L31). Pre-existing; worth exporting one named type eventually, not in this diff. --- ## Lens 3 — UI/UX ### `Broken` (verify in browser) — `h-4` on the `+N More` button clips its own text ```tsx

aria-label={t("see_count_more_responsibilities", {
